title: Live three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography of left ventricular intramyocardial hydatid cyst
case_text:
An 18-year-old male was referred to us for chest discomfort. A physical examination showed normal findings. The chest X-ray was also normal. ECG showed sinus rhythm and ischaemic changes in apico-infero-posterior myocardium. Two-dimensional-TTE (2DTTE) (Supplementary data online, Movie S1) showed a single, large oval cyst (39 x 56 x 38 mm). The edge was well defined (Panel A), it was intramyocardial and fluid-filled. It was located in the infero-postero-apical segment, protruding into the pericardium but mainly bulging into the left ventricular cavity (Supplementary data online, Movie S2). L3DTTE (Supplementary data online, Movie S3) allowed cropping of this cystic mass in transverse, sagittal (Panel B), and oblique planes, showing an apico-infero-posterior intramyocardial ellipsoid cystic mass with liquid content and well-defined edges. These data showed a life-threatening mass, mainly due to the possibility of intrapericardial and/or left ventricular rupture as well as systemic embolization. Chest computed tomography (CT) (Panel C) confirmed the presence of a left ventricular intramyocardial cyst and also a multivesicular hepatic cyst. The patient was referred to cardiac surgery. Surgical findings (Panel D) confirmed the accuracy of the preoperative echocardiography. The postoperative course was uneventful and the patient was discharged in stable condition. Three months later, his hepatic cyst was removed with no complications.
Two-dimensional TTE remain the widely used imaging modality in cardiac echinococcosis, L3DTTE was shown to complement 2DTTE by displaying the 3D volume of the cyst and spatial relation to the neighbouring cardiac structures. This information is vital, especially since surgical removal of the cyst is the treatment of choice for this uncommon, but life-threatening disease.
(Panel A) TTE: zoomed apex with egg-shaped hydatid mass. (Panel B) Live three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiogram, zoomed and cropped view. (Panel C) CT scan revealed a well defined, non-enhancing, oval hypodense mass. (Panel D) Intraoperative situs. The cystic mass is seen in the muscle of the left ventricular apex. The cyst was opened and its content aspirated. Cystic material removed. A large defect before its reconstruction.

You are an expert clinician–educator in tropical and infectious diseases.
Your job is to transform a published clinical case report into a standardized admission diagnostic teaching case following the Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology.

In terms of style, model your output on NEJM’s Clinicopathologic Conferences ("Case Records of the Massachusetts General Hospital").

RULES (Read Carefully — No Exceptions):
1. SOURCE FIDELITY:
   - Extract facts ONLY from the supplied case report.
   - Do NOT invent, embellish, or smooth out missing clinical data.
   - Never extrapolate findings not explicitly mentioned.

2. THE ADMISSION BREAKPOINT PRINCIPLE (CRITICAL):
   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Echinococcosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: cardiac and hepatic hydatid cysts
